title: Paul: Apostle and Theologian
welcome_lead: Walk with Paul from the Damascus road through the cities of the Mediterranean as he writes the letters that would shape Christian theology.
meta_desc: A-Level New Testament Studies adventure on Paul: chronology, the seven undisputed letters, justification, and the New Perspective.
final_note: You have surveyed Paul's life, the disputed letter corpus, and the New Perspective debate.

walkthroughs.body_html: Paul's career can be roughly dated from the Gallio inscription at Delphi (c.51-52 AD), which places him in Corinth (Acts 18). His undisputed letters likely span c.50-58 AD: 1 Thessalonians earliest, Romans around 57-58. He died, tradition says, under Nero c.64-67 AD. Acts and the letters together trace three missionary journeys.

In Galatians, written to Gentile believers being pressed to adopt circumcision, Paul insists 'a person is not justified by works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ' (Gal 2:16). Romans expands this: all have sinned (3:23); justification is by grace through faith (3:24-25); the resulting life is in the Spirit (Romans 8).

E. P. Sanders's Paul and Palestinian Judaism (1977) argued that Second Temple Judaism was a religion of 'covenantal nomism', not works-righteousness. James D. G. Dunn coined 'the New Perspective on Paul' in a 1982 lecture. N. T. Wright in What Saint Paul Really Said (1997) recasts justification as covenant membership marked out by faith, with implications for ecumenical theology.

options: Acts 2
Acts 9

mcqs.q: What is the doctrine of the Trinity?
options: The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
Christians believe in three different gods.
God is one being existing in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) — distinct in person but united in essence; Christians remain monotheistic.
Secularisation means the separation of church and state.

mcqs.q: Why do Jews not accept Jesus as the Messiah?
options: Because Jews believe Jesus never existed.
Secularisation means the separation of church and state.
Because Jesus was crucified, and the Messiah cannot die.
Because the Jewish Messiah is expected to bring peace, rebuild the Temple and restore Israel — events the Jewish tradition holds Jesus did not accomplish.

mcqs.q: What does the secularisation thesis claim?
options: The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
That as societies modernise, religion declines in social significance — though sociologists now debate this, since global religion has not declined uniformly.
Secularisation means the separation of church and state.
Secularisation means everyone in modern countries is now atheist.
